2.content:
This SOW covers Bristlecone’s implementation engagement for Google’s Global Template Design for Silicon COT Supply Chain, focused on establishing a standardized global design, execution approach, and supporting governance for deployment across the target supply chain landscape.

- Define and sign off a global business process template using industry best practices, fit-to-standard workshops, and stakeholder participation across key sites.
- Deliver the design foundation for execution, including integration data mapping and validation, key design decisions, baseline configuration, RICEFW identification, and strategies for testing, training, and data migration.
- Enable controlled rollout through project governance, organizational change management, phased delivery, and coordinated stakeholder engagement across onsite and offshore teams.

Any deferred scope decisions, delivery dependencies, and planning assumptions for this engagement are captured in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Google is undertaking a global template design for its Silicon COT supply chain to standardize core processes across foundry, OSAT, manufacturing, and distribution operations while accommodating local business and regulatory requirements. The current landscape requires a clearer AS-IS baseline across procurement flows, subcontracting settlement, batch and lot traceability, enterprise structure, and supply collaboration processes involving external partners such as TSMC and OSAT providers.

Key pain points include fragmented process ownership across global and regional teams, gaps in master data harmonization, unresolved system and organizational dependencies, and incomplete alignment between business processes, integration flows, and reporting needs. The engagement is intended to establish a fit-to-standard global design, define the target operating model, validate technical and data mappings across SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, and Kinaxis, and provide the governance and execution foundation for a controlled phased rollout.

<IMAGE id="689305094e2e"/>

3.2.content:
- Establish and sign off a global process template for the Silicon COT supply chain based on fit-to-standard design and stakeholder alignment.
- Baseline current-state processes, enterprise structure, master data, and integration flows across front-end and back-end operations.
- Define the target-state business processes, organizational model, and design assumptions required for the COT operating model.
- Map end-to-end data flows, technical dependencies, and integration requirements across SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, and Kinaxis.
- Identify configuration, reporting, traceability, and RICEFW-related design requirements needed for downstream execution.
- Develop a sprint-based execution approach with agreed scope priorities, dependencies, milestones, and governance.

3.3.content:
The target-state process flow is designed to support a standardized Silicon COT supply chain from demand and procurement through subcontract manufacturing, traceability, and reporting. Google’s future-state model will align global process definitions across foundry and OSAT operations, harmonize enterprise and master data structures, and define controlled integration points for planning and supply collaboration systems.

At a high level, the to-be flow covers demand and supply collaboration inputs, purchase order execution with external manufacturing partners, lot-controlled material movement and genealogy tracking from wafer through finished goods, subcontracting and yield recording, goods movement and cost capture in SAP S/4HANA, and downstream reporting for cost, yield, and traceability. The process will also define system boundaries between lot-level collaboration and unit-level analytics, with governance over regional variations, compliance requirements, and dependency management.

<IMAGE id="ab28c1ba0ba6"/>

4.1.content: The engagement covers the Silicon COT supply chain design and implementation activities for Google operations and partner-connected flows across North America and Taiwan. In-scope locations include Google Hub and warehouse operations, together with external manufacturing and supply collaboration touchpoints involving TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL in Taiwan. Delivery will be executed through a combined onsite North America and offshore model as set out in this SOW.

4.2.content: In scope are the end-to-end Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain processes required to define and enable the global template. These include constrained supply planning with yield considerations, demand and supply alignment, procurement execution with external manufacturing partners, subcontracting-related process flows, material master alignment, batch and lot traceability, inventory visibility, goods movement support, and analytics inputs needed to improve the ASIC commit process. The scope also includes current-state discovery, fit-gap assessment, target-state process design, and validation of business process flows across foundry, OSAT, manufacturing, and distribution touchpoints.

4.3.content: Technical scope includes solution design, configuration, and integration activities across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and associated interface components required for the Silicon COT template. In scope are incremental delta interfaces, use of Google’s existing integration framework for machines planning where applicable, adaptation of existing data templates for Silicon planning needs, and BTP-IS-based integration between SAP S/4HANA and E2Open. The engagement also includes design and build activities for Kinaxis data consumption from E2Open, including capacity information and contract manufacturer data for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL, plus resource master, yield, and unit-of-measure integrations. SAP to PLM and SAP to BigQuery integration points are included for design validation and downstream analytics planning, with detailed interface design to be confirmed during discovery.

4.4.content: Services in scope include project management, fit-gap analysis, to-be process design, business process design documentation, functional specifications for approved custom development, configuration and build, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance testing support, regression testing, performance testing, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, hypercare, organizational change management, and knowledge transfer to the support team. Bristlecone will provide cross-functional delivery across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and integration workstreams in a phased Agile model covering Explore, Build, and Deploy.

4.5.content: The applications in scope are SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open. Within Kinaxis, the in-scope functional areas are Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and Data Integration. Within SAP S/4HANA, the in-scope areas are Production Planning (PP), Materials Management (MM), and process integration required to support the Silicon COT template. Controlling-related requirements will be supported where needed for process alignment, with Google responsible for staffing the CO function.

4.7.content:
- Global rollout beyond the design and implementation scope defined for this 10-month engagement.
- Net-new replacement of Google’s existing integration framework where reuse and extension are sufficient.
- Custom development not identified, assessed, and approved through the agreed design and change control process.
- Production support services beyond the defined hypercare period.
- Direct ownership or staffing of Google-controlled functions, including client-side CO staffing.
- Unit-level MES or test data implementation beyond defined boundary validation and interface assessment.
- Activities for plants, regions, applications, or process areas not expressly identified in this SOW.
- Changes driven by post-design scope expansion, additional partner onboarding, or new interface requirements unless approved through Change Management.
